topic: Model Context Protocol (MCP) — connecting AI assistants to your data
visual_rule: Every visual is tied to a narration sentence and a sourced claim. No generic AI imagery, no stock processor photos, no unrelated robots. Where a photograph does not exist for the concept, an original animated diagram (labelled illustrative) represents the fact.

scenes.narration: AI assistants are trapped behind information silos.
scenes.claim: AI assistants are constrained by isolation from data — trapped behind information silos and legacy systems.
scenes.source: S1 — Anthropic, Introducing the Model Context Protocol (Nov 25, 2024)
scenes.visual_requirement: Center-screen kinetic typography stating the problem. Two phrases landing sequentially so the viewer reads in sync with the VO.
scenes.visual_treatment: Kinetic typography: slide-up + opacity reveal, 150px w800, first phrase textPrimary, second phrase accent. Flat bg, no photograph.
scenes.relevance: Typeset the hook sentence itself; nothing unrelated shown.

scenes.narration: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol is one open standard connecting AI to your data.
scenes.claim: MCP is a universal, open standard for connecting AI systems with data sources.
scenes.visual_requirement: Article-highlight card: marker stroke draws left-to-right across the key phrase as it is spoken; source URL printed on the card.
scenes.visual_treatment: Surface panel (radius 20), headline above, key phrase 'ONE OPEN STANDARD' in accent with a 7px marker-stroke draw-on (14 frames), citation line with the official source URL at card bottom.
scenes.relevance: Visual evidence tied to the sourced claim; source URL on screen per article-highlights skill.

scenes.narration: An MCP server exposes your data; an MCP client like Claude connects to it.
scenes.claim: Developers expose data through MCP servers or build MCP clients that connect; MCP works like USB-C for AI — one standard port.
scenes.visual_requirement: Animated diagram: client node → connector → server node → data-source nodes, connectors drawn on, client emphasized with a push-in.
scenes.visual_treatment: Original animated diagram (labelled illustrative): three surface-filled nodes with stroke borders, 5px stroke connectors drawn via evolvePath-style stroke-dash, one camera push-in on the client node, pan across sources. No photograph zoomed (cinematic-camera rule).
scenes.relevance: Diagrams the server/client relationship the sentence states, using the official MCP roles as the factual basis.

scenes.narration: Pre-built MCP servers exist for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Postgres and Puppeteer.
scenes.claim: Pre-built MCP servers exist for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres and Puppeteer.
scenes.visual_requirement: Terminal insert: character-by-character typing of an MCP server stdio config block with a blinking cursor; server names listed on screen.
scenes.visual_treatment: Dark terminal chrome (#0A0A1A), traffic lights, JetBrains Mono, lines appear sequentially (slide-in + reveal), highlighted command line in accent, blinking block cursor (500ms cycle). Below, a server-name list.
scenes.relevance: Shows an actual MCP configuration shape the user would write; grounds the claim in a real, plausible implementation.

scenes.narration: Build once, integrate everywhere. AI finally reaches your data.
scenes.claim: MCP enables building once and integrating everywhere, giving AI systems access to the data where it lives.
scenes.visual_requirement: Summary card with the diagram settling to a stable center composition; credits with both source URLs at bottom left.
scenes.visual_treatment: Large kinetic typography 'BUILD ONCE · INTEGRATE EVERYWHERE', accent close line, final push-in to diagram center, hold. Credits cite both sources.
scenes.relevance: Restates the single coherent takeaway; both sources credited on screen.

relevance_gate.rule: A missing relevant photograph is NOT replaced by an unrelated image. Original motion graphics are used instead and labelled illustrative.
